newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Opp'n says can accept bank merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Opp'n says can accept bank merger.

text.p: Australia's Labor Opposition said on Tuesday it had no problem with the proposed merger of St George Bank Ltd and Advance Bank Ltd.
"I think that's one that we can probably accept," opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans told reporters.
"But it's important that the basic principle of the major banks not being allowed to further contract be accepted."
The government is still to comment on the A$2.65 billion merger, announced on Monday, but anti-monopolies body the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission will examine the proposal.
Evans said any further mergers could reduce competition to unacceptable levels.

"Our concern would be that if any further mergers take place as a result of the Wallis inquiry (into banking) or further policy changes, there'll be all sorts of pressure to dramatically reduce the number of retail banking outlets around the country," he said.
"It simply won't be in the community interest, quite apart from the basic worry of reduced competition."
ACCC chairman Allan Fels has said he would be concerned if bank mergers left any state market without one regional bank.
St George Bank and Advance Bank are both New South Wales-based banks, but there would still be two regional banks in the state if they merged.
The former State Bank of New South Wales is currently operating as Colonial State Bank as part of the Colonial Mutual Group.
St George Bank is offering A$7.30 for each Advance Bank share.
